cardChanges.summary: Read the US BES878 Q26 booklet. Added supported manufacturer claims: dial 1 finest/30 coarsest, upper-burr adjustment procedure (p18), single vs dual-wall baskets and doses, bean freshness, the fast-shot extraction guide and troubleshooting row, burr cleaning, the green-bean warning and the warranty scope. Added booklet evidence to grind-settings-start-15. Added a merchant claim for the pre-1926 PDC burr SP0001801. Updated the notes on the upper-burr procedure, factory position and warranty unknowns.

Read the US BES870 X26 booklet. Added supported manufacturer claims: dial 1–16 with a starting setting of 5, the upper-burr adjustment procedure (p21), basket guidance, dose and extraction targets, the fast-shot troubleshooting row, bean freshness, burr cleaning, the green-bean warning and the warranty scope. Added a merchant claim for the pre-1926 PDC burr SP0001801 and an unknown for the factory position. Resolved the upper-burr-tool dispute as tool-free from the booklet. Updated the notes on the upper-burr procedure.

learned: Breville presents the upper burr as an owner feature, not a service-only part. Both US booklets say it extends the grind range because 'some types of coffee may require a wider grind range', and recommend one adjustment at a time (barista-express/upper-burr-adjustment-documented, barista-pro/upper-burr-adjustment-documented).

No tool is needed. The burr is turned and lifted out by its wire handle, and the included Allen key is for the shower-screen seal. This resolves the earlier retailer dispute (barista-express/upper-burr-tool).

The dials run from finest 1 to coarsest 16 on the Express (Breville suggests starting at 5) and from finest 1 to coarsest 30 on the Pro (default 15). A reader stuck at 1 has used up the whole dial (barista-express/grind-dial-1-finest-16-coarsest, barista-pro/grind-dial-1-finest-30-coarsest, barista-pro/grind-settings-start-15).

Breville's own fast-shot causes are grind too coarse, too little coffee and tamping too lightly. The burrs are not on that list, so the upper-burr step comes after those checks (barista-express/troubleshooting-runs-too-quickly, barista-pro/troubleshooting-runs-too-quickly).

Bean freshness is Breville's first-line check. It recommends a 'Roasted On' date and use 5–20 days after roasting, and the Pro booklet explicitly warns that stale coffee 'may pour too quickly' (barista-pro/beans-roasted-on-5-20-days, barista-express/beans-roasted-on-5-20-days).

Dual-wall (pressurised) baskets regulate pressure 'regardless of the grind, dose and tamp pressure or freshness' and are meant for pre-ground coffee. Single-wall baskets are for fresh beans, so a reader diagnosing grind should be on single-wall (barista-pro/baskets-single-vs-dual-wall, barista-express/baskets-single-vs-dual-wall).

The targets are 8–11 g (single) and 16–19 g (double), with the tamper cap level with the rim after tamping and a 25–30 s shot. A shot that starts flowing in under 7 s (Pro) or 1–6 s (Express) is under-extracted (barista-express/dose-and-extraction-targets, barista-pro/extraction-guide-fast-shot).

Breville says cleaning the burrs 'removes oil build-up on the burrs which can impede performance', which makes it a free step before touching the burr position (barista-pro/burr-cleaning-cycle, barista-express/burr-cleaning-cycle).

Breville warns against grinding green or under-roasted beans, which can damage the burrs. This is relevant to readers chasing very light roasts on the built-in grinder (barista-pro/no-green-or-under-roasted-beans, barista-express/no-green-or-under-roasted-beans).

Two upper-burr part numbers exist depending on the production date code: SP0001801 before the 1926 PDC and SP0027464 from 2019 week 26 on, read from the sticker underneath. This rests on a merchant listing only (barista-express/upper-burr-part-sp0001801, barista-express/upper-burr-part-sp0027464).

In one owner report, cleaning plus moving the internal burr from 2 to 1 fixed a refurbished Pro before the free replacement burr Breville offered had arrived (barista-pro/owner-refurb-upper-burr-fix).
The booklet's warranty text covers defects in materials, workmanship or function. It says nothing about burr adjustment (barista-pro/warranty-scope).
unknowns: The upper-burr number range and the factory position on the BES870 and BES878. Neither booklet states them, and the '6' default appears only in blog posts and forum snippets. This matters because readers need to know how many steps finer they have left. Ask Breville US support, or have a human photograph the burr ring on a stock machine.
Whether Breville warns about burr contact (chirping or clashing) at the finest upper-burr position. Neither booklet mentions it.

Whether adjusting or replacing the upper burr affects the Breville US warranty. The booklet presents adjustment as a feature, but the full terms on breville.com were not read and support was not asked.
The US price and availability of genuine upper burrs (SP0001801 and SP0027464). Only Australian merchant listings were read (AUD $184.95 and $241.95), and the ECS US page returned 429.
Whether the earliest Barista Express units had a non-adjustable upper burr. This came only from a search snippet attributed to PERC Coffee, and the fetched page didn't contain it.
How to recognise a worn built-in burr, and Breville's guidance on burr life. Breville gives none, and general burr-life articles are not specific to these machines.
Whether the older BES870 O21 booklet has different upper-burr text. It was not re-read in this pass.

competitors.says: Gives clear removal steps for the top burr, but says to go 'coarser' when shots run fast at the finest setting, which is backwards. It gives no range, no factory position, no burr-contact warning, and no check of beans, basket and dose first.

States a factory inner-burr setting of 6 and advises at most 2 steps at a time. It does not cite Breville (which recommends one adjustment at a time), name the models, or cover burr contact, warranty, part date codes or worn burrs.

Owner thread where advice splits between shimming, 'don't touch the internal burr', returning the machine and buying a grinder. The owner's actual fix was cleaning plus internal burr 1, and Breville offered a free upper burr. There is no diagnosis order.
